prompt:
A student measures the length of a wooden beam using a metre rule.
(a) Explain how parallax error can occur when using a metre rule to make a measurement. [2]
(b) The student consistently looks at the scale from an angle to the right of the mark. State and explain whether this parallax error is systematic or random. [1]
(c) State one practical technique to eliminate or minimize parallax error when reading a scale. [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: Part (a): There is a gap / physical separation between the markings on the rule and the object being measured.
Part (a): If the line of sight is not perpendicular to the scale, the end of the object projects onto an incorrect scale division.
Part (b): Systematic error, because viewing consistently from the same angle shifts all readings in the same direction.
Part (c): Position the eye directly perpendicular to the scale mark (or place the rule on its edge so the markings touch the object, or use a plane mirror behind the pointer).

hints: In part (a), mention the physical gap between scale and object and non-perpendicular viewing.
In part (b), does consistent viewing produce a one-way shift or scatter?
In part (c), how should your eye be positioned relative to the scale?
solution: (a) A gap exists between the scale markings and the object. If the observer's line of sight is not perpendicular to the scale, the edge of the object appears aligned with an incorrect scale division. (b) It is a systematic error because viewing consistently from the same angle shifts all readings in the same direction. (c) View the scale perpendicularly with the line of sight at 90 degrees to the scale (or place the rule on its edge).
teacher_walkthrough: (a) Parallax occurs when there is a distance between the scale and the measurement surface. An oblique viewing angle projects the pointer/edge onto the wrong graduation mark.
(b) Because the student consistently views from the right, the apparent shift is always in the same direction, making it a systematic error.
(c) Position the eye perpendicular (at 90 degrees) to the scale, or place the rule on edge so the markings touch the surface directly.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored detailed explanation of parallax error mechanism, directional classification, and avoidance.
